title: VM Scale Sets vs Availability Sets
description: Choose between VM Scale Sets and Availability Sets for high availability.

data.text: You need to run 10 identical VMs for a stateless web farm. The VMs must be highly available and automatically scale based on CPU usage. Should you use VM Scale Sets or Availability Sets?
Use **VM Scale Sets** for stateless workloads that need auto-scaling. Availability Sets are legacy; VM Scale Sets provide the same fault domain distribution plus automatic scaling and orchestration.

data.title: Azure CLI - Create VM Scale Set with Auto-scaling
data.code:
# Create VM Scale Set
az vmss create \
  --resource-group 'rg-webfarm' \
  --name 'vmss-web' \
  --image 'UbuntuLTS' \
  --vm-sku 'Standard_D2s_v3' \
  --instance-count 5 \
  --upgrade-policy-mode automatic \
  --admin-username azureuser \
  --generate-ssh-keys

# Configure auto-scaling
az monitor autoscale create \
  --resource-group 'rg-webfarm' \
  --resource 'vmss-web' \
  --resource-type 'Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets' \
  --name 'autoscale-web' \
  --min-count 2 \
  --max-count 20 \
  --count 5

data.text: VM Scale Sets provide **automatic scaling**, **load balancing**, and **fault domain distribution** out of the box. Availability Sets only provide fault domains without scaling.
